lines.text: Have you ever wondered why are the landforms on the Earth so different? One reason for this is
over time. Earth's surface changes due to internal forces, like tectonic activity and external
forces, like wind and water. These forces have transformed the appearance of the Earth over
millions of years. Weathering and erosion are the natural processes by which the rocks are
broken down and the shape of different landforms is changed.
6.1 Weathering
Weathering is the breaking down of rocks into smaller pieces on the surface of the Earth in its
place by the agents of weathering.
